texts.Braid hair curves:
Braid hair curves

Braids require quite a lot of points per curve in order to create the shape of a braid. Find the lowest possible subdivision in the node to create a nice shape buyt also keeping the hairstyle optimized for viewport display. 

Shape controls if the braid should be more thin at the root or at the tip

The Hair Tie parameter points to an object (hairband) that is instanced at the end of each braid.
texts.Clump hair curves (small clumps):
Clump hair curves (small clumps)

This node creates smaller clumps out of the existing clumps. 

The Guide Distance parameter has a smaller value than the previous Clump Hair Curves node in order to create smaller clumps.

By setting Existing Guide Map to FALSE and setting Clump Offset to another value than zero, the clumps start diverging from their original direction. This is a good way of breaking up the shape of the hair.
texts.Curl Hair Curves:
Curl Hair Curves

Guide Index ha no incoming data in order to control the size of the curls with the parameter Guide Distance. 

Adding some subdivision is useful since curls ususally need more hair points in order to create the curled shape.

Curl Start is set to 1 so that the curl does not start directly at the root.

Factor Start and End controls the radius of the curl

Frequency controls the amount of curls along the hair strands.

Random Offset controls the thickness of the curl "band". By using a Spline Parameter node and a color ramp it is possible to control how much offset there should be along each hair curve.
texts.Displace Hair Curves:
Displace Hair Curves

When creating braids, the interpolation of the hairs can cause intersection wit the scalp, which makes the character look a bit bald. This issue is fixed by pushing out the hair closest to the root from the scalp.

This node is much faster to use compared to Shrinkwrap Hair Curves when you know exactly which part of the hair you want to deform.
texts.Duplicate Hair Curves:
Duplicate Hair Curves

This node will duplicate the hair curves to a single strand of hair. This is useful when you want to be very specific about how the hair should be shaped. 

Since it only spawns a couple of hairs around each hair curve it is very cheap to compute.
texts.Hair Curve Noise:
Hair Curve Noise

The purpose of this setup is to create some fly away hairs. By changing the value of the parameter Offset per Curve, each hair gets an unique noise shape. 

Distance controls how much the hairs should deform.

It is important to set a fairly low frequency of the noise for the hair in order to get bigger noise shapes.

Content:

Cyberpunk hair
This setup is intended to showcase the workflow of creating a hair setup in the modifier tab. It uses some vertex groups to control hair parameters. This can be useful for artist that are not familiar with node graphs, but gives less detailed control compared to to the geometry nodes setups.
    
Long hair
This hairstyle uses two separate hair objects in order to separate the grooming in different parts. Look at the notes in the geometry nodes tab to get more insight about the hair setup. 

Curly hair
Look at the notes in the geometry nodes tab to get more insight about the hair setup.

Braids hair
Look at the notes in the geometry nodes tab to get more insight about the hair setup. 
------------------------------

Notes:

When grooming, it is best to turn off all other hair collections in order to get a responsive grooming experience. You can do that with the little checkbox to the right of the collection in the outliner.
    
In order to groom a hair object, select it and then choose "Sculpt Mode" from the object interaction mode menu in the top left corner.

When testing the nodes in the Geometry Nodes workspace (tab at the top of the UI), you can mute nodes witht the hotkey "M" to see the influence they have on the hairstyle.

Hairstyles like braids and curls requires addition subdivision of the curves. Default is 1, but has been changed to 3 in Properties > Render Properties > Curves.

Each hairstyle is attached to a growth mesh, which is just a single sided haircap. The growth mesh is separated in two mesh island. The hairs will interpolate based on which mesh island the guide hairs belong to. It also has a vertex group called "parting". This is used to move hairs closer to the parting line in order to avoid a "bald look" at the parting line.

In Eevee, the best display mode of curves are Strip instead of Strand, which is default. This can be changed in Properties > Render Properties > Curves.

The human haid normally has 90,000-150,000 hairs. The amount of hair has been kept less than that to keep the viewport and grooming running smoothly since there are multiple hairstyles in this file.
texts.Interpolate hair curves:
Interpolate hair curves

This node generates more hair curves that aligns to the shape of the guide curves. Surface object and Surface UV Map parameters are important in order for the node to generate the hair curves correctly. 

The part by mesh island parameter is important for hairstyles that requires hair parting. The growth mesh should be separate in multiple mesh island. Each hair curve will interpolate per each mesh island. 

The Guide index output is used by other nodes (such as Clump hair curves) in order to interpolate hair curves correctly.

Posson Disk Distribution will generate hair with more even spacing, but will take longer time to calculate.

Viewport Amount is connected to the Group Input, which makes the user able to control the parameter from the modifier.
texts.Long hair clumping:
Clump hair curves

Clumping is very useful for creating a natural look for the hair. 

The Guide Distance parameter sets the size of each clump.

Shape parameter < 0 affects more of the root and values > 0 affects the tip more.

Tip spread parameter controls the width of the tip.

The Guide Index parameter needs data from the Interpolate Hair Curves node in order to interpolate hair to the correct guide hair. When the data is disconnected, the hairs starts intersecting with the head. This is most notably when using local view on the hair.
texts.Notes:

When Guide Index is plugged into Curl Hair Curves, it seems that it is not possible to edit the size of the curls with Guide Distance

texts.Notes on fly away hair:
Separate geometry

In order to increase performance this nodes separates out the hair that will be deformed. This makes it faster to calculate, but changes the hair index order of the hair. 

By changing the index order, nodes that requires Guide Index data (such as Clump Hair Curves) will not work properly.
texts.Roll hair curves info:
Roll hair curves info


Roll hair curves is useful for creating a bend at the end of the hair curve. 

By placing the node before Interpolate hair curves, it becomes much faster to calculate
texts.Set hair curve profile info:
Set hair curve profile 

This node sets the radius (thickness) of each hair. The shape parameter controls if the root or the tip should be more thin

import bpy

node_tree_name = 'hair'

    if not node.select:
        continue
    node.use_custom_color = True
    node.color = (0.20666, 0.154987, 0.0521326)
texts.Shrinkwrap Hair Curves:
Shrinkwrap Hair Curves

The purpose of this node is iterate over any hair point that is intersecting with the head and push it outside of the head surface in order to avoid intersection.

By setting the parameter Above Surface to 0, only points that are below the surface is affected.
texts.Smooth Hair Curves:
Smooth Hair Curves

Since the flare ends can be a bit noisy in the shape, it is useful to take the FlareParameter output from the Braid Hair Curves and plug it into a Smooth Hair Curve node.

Preserve Length takes some extra time to calculate, so only Lock Tips are activated in this setup.
texts.Snap hair to parting edges:
Snap hair to parting edges

This is a custom node group created to minimize the scalp visibility at the hair parting

The growth mesh should contain a vertex group that defines the parting area and defined in the "Parting Attribute" parameter. The hair curves within the proximity will snap to the partin area.

Since the hair shader has some tranaparency in the root, the effect of this node is more visible with solid viewport shading.
texts.Trim Hair Curves:
Trim Hair Curves

This node will shrink or grow each hair curve. By using the parameter "Random offset", the length of each hair curve will differ. This will give the hair a more natural look in combination with Clump hair Curves.
